subject: On-prem deployment: evidence access windows & operator witness redlines
messages:

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixtherapeutics.com>

Subject: Private install — evidence access windows and operator witnessing

Hi Stephanie / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're progressing internal approvals to move from evaluation to a private on-prem deployment for the clinical inference workload. Legal and InfoSec have a handful of asks before procurement can sign:

- A clear definition of the "evidence access window" for witness operations (how long Redwood engineers can access environment during onboarding / snapshots).
- Confirmation that operator access is time-limited (ephemeral creds) and logging/audit exports will be provided.
- Options for an escrow-like acceptance: sealed snapshot deposit vs witnessed runbook execution (we need details on both).

I've attached our RFI checklist (helix-rfi-checklist.pdf) and a short summary of the compliance board's questions. Can you propose redline language for the MSA/Order Form exhibits and an estimated timeline for approvals? We have a procurement deadline on 2026-11-26.

Best,
Emma Ross
Head of IT Compliance
Helix Therapeutics

Attachment: helix-rfi-checklist.pdf (PDF, 92 KB)

Emma — thanks for the clear checklist and timeline. We can support both sealed-snapshot and witnessed execution paths; each has tradeoffs for timeline and evidence strength. Proposed next steps:

1) Redwood legal (cc'd) to propose concrete MSA exhibit language for a limited "Witnessed Acceptance" and an alternate "Sealed Snapshot Deposit" clause. Expect a first-pass redline within 3 business days.
2) Engineering to provide a runbook excerpt showing exact actions that will be performed during witness window (we'll include required logs and artifacts). Ben, can you attach that runbook excerpt?
3) Ops to confirm that operator sessions will be ephemeral, MFA-enforced, and that exports (audit trail + snapshot checksums) will be delivered to Helix within 48 hours of the window.

We can align procurement timeline to your 11/26 target if legal gets the exhibit draft by 11/15 and procurement runs a short review. I'll coordinate with Aditya on the specific redlines for the Order Form and Exhibit language.

– Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private install — proposed technical exhibit text and options

Emma / Stephanie — attaching a short draft exhibit and a technical runbook excerpt for the witness flow. Key items in the draft:

- Evidence access window: defined as a scheduled, mutually agreed window (typical 4–8 hours) during which assigned Redwood operators may perform onboarding tasks. We propose a maximum of two windows for the initial deployment and one optional revalidation window within 90 days.
- Operator access scope: ephemeral credentials issued via customer-managed Jump host; session recording and audit exports delivered as gzipped logs within 48 hours.
- Snapshot deposit option: Redwood may create a sealed snapshot (SHA256 checksum) and deposit to a neutral escrow agent (third-party) with delivery instructions to Helix upon contract termination or mutually agreed trigger.
- Proof-of-execution: runbook output + signed operational affidavit from Redwood engineer.

I've included a short doc (proposed-exhibit-g-draft.docx) with suggested redline snippets that Aditya can refine for legal-mandated wording. Two clarifying questions for Helix: 1) Do you require third-party notary vs. Helix witness? 2) Is the escrow agent required to be in the US?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-exhibit-g-draft.docx (DOCX, 38 KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@helixtherapeutics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Private install — MSA/Order Form redlines and timeline

Emma / team — following Ben's technical draft, Redwood legal recommends the following high-level redlines to surface in the MSA/Order Form exhibits:

1) Limited Access Clause: operator access during "Witnessed Acceptance" is time-boxed, logged, and limited to pre-defined runbook steps. Access revokes automatically at the end of the window.
2) No Persistent Key Transfer: Redwood will not hand over long-term private keys or root credentials. For any key escrow/handback, a sealed snapshot + agreed handback procedure is required.
3) Audit Artifacts: Redwood shall deliver audit exports (session recordings, log excerpts, snapshot checksums) as read-only artifacts within 48 hours. Delivery method and retention period to be stated in Order Form exhibit.
4) Liability Carveouts: limited to operator negligence during witnessed ops; standard MSA liability caps to apply.
5) Witnessing Options: provide primary path (Helix witness via on-site presence or secure Zoom with recorded session) and alternative path (sealed snapshot deposited with neutral escrow agent). Specify jurisdiction for escrow agent in Order Form (we recommend listing both US and EU options).

Timeline: Redwood legal will circulate a redline to the MSA and a draft Order Form exhibit by 2026-11-15 COB. Please confirm if that timeline meets your procurement window. Once Helix provides feedback, we can aim for signature by 2026-11-25 if no major commercial changes are required.

I'll attach the legal redline in the next message; for now, please confirm the two clarifying items Ben raised (notary requirement and escrow jurisdiction).

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
